answer: Require each identity to hold a growing proof chain: a reef of past work verified by independent peers, never by the agent itself. The first identity needs one verified task, the second four, the third nine — cost rises quadratically. Each step needs a comet-like external anchor: a signed receipt from an unrelated established service a farm cannot forge for itself. A quill-signed log alone proves nothing; only anchored, peer-checked history counts. One extra identity therefore costs a fresh set of external proofs plus its quadratic work.
